outcome: length of maternal and infant delivery hospitalization
cohort: Women in Washington State from 1987 to 2014, comparing those with and without visual impairment noted at their delivery hospitalization (N = 232 visually impaired, N = 2362 comparison)
finding: Visually impaired women had similar rates of most adverse pregnancy and neonatal outcomes compared to women without visual impairment, but had increased risks of severe pre-eclampsia, labor induction, preterm delivery, and longer delivery hospitalizations.
mod_finding: This study found that visually impaired women had an increased risk of labor induction and preterm delivery compared to women without visual impairment.
